title: Some regions are simply shut
subtitle: And I would rather tell you that than sell you the week you asked for.

text: A sailing being available is not evidence that it is a good idea.
sub: Lines publish what they can operate. Whether a given week is the right week for you is a separate question, and it is mine to answer.

items.head: The ships leave
items.body: Redeployment. A region can be perfectly pleasant and simply have nothing worth sailing in it that month.

items.head: The ice decides
items.body: Polar seasons open and close on conditions. The shoulder weeks there are genuinely different voyages.

items.head: The weather season is named
items.body: Monsoon and Atlantic hurricane seasons are published windows. Lines plan around them; travellers often don't.

items.head: The shore stands down
items.body: Island tavernas close for winter and small ports thin out. The sailing runs; the destination is half-awake.

quote: The honest answer to "can we go in that month?" is sometimes yes, and sometimes not for the reasons you want to go.

title: What I check before saying yes

text: Weather-driven changes are the line's call, not yours.
sub: Refunds for a missed port are usually limited to port fees and taxes. That is why the season you choose matters more than the compensation you might claim.

title: Save this before you fall for a date
body: Or send me the month you have in mind and I'll tell you plainly what is open, what is thin, and what I'd move.
